title: Shimon Efrati
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Hyman relates in connection with Ketubot 103b that Rabbi, before his death, said: “Yosef Chafni and Shimon Efrati served me in my life, and they will serve me in my death.” It was thought that they would attend to his burial. Later it became apparent that they had died before Rabbi, and his meaning was understood: they would serve him there.
And in the Yerushalmi there, chapter 2, halakhah 3, he is called Yosef Efrati.

notes.text: Hyman cites Ketubot 103b; the matching account in the checked text is on 103a. His final Yerushalmi name Yosef Efrati is retained as a reported variant, distinct from Shimon Efrati.

No new primary scalar was returned. The earlier recorded Ketubot comparison locates the account at 103a beside supplied 103b; that consultation is inherited, not newly inspected here. The supplied Jerusalem Talmud locator remains chapter 2, halakhah 3. Yosef Chafni, Shimon Efrati and the final Yosef Efrati are different transmitted forms, not harmonized identities. Hyman narrates the death and burial episode; the implied service there is not an independently admitted historical or theological conclusion.

The consulted scan of Hyman, volume III, printed pp. 1155–1156, gives כתובות קג. (103a), whereas the supplied text retained in the translation has קג: (103b). Davidson Ketubot 103a directly contains both the instruction about Yosef Chafni and Shimon Efrati and the explanation that observers saw their biers precede Rabbi’s. The printed continuation retains the Yerushalmi locator פ״ב ה״ג and the name Yosef Efrati. The directly consulted parallel is Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 12:3: its Hebrew has יוסף אפרתי and יוסה חפני, while Guggenheimer’s English gives Yose Ephrati and Joseph from Haifa. The different names and chapter locators remain visible without an identity merger. The earlier notes describe the supplied transcription and the state before this printed-page and fresh parallel inspection.
